subject: society
topic: The 'Just-World Hypothesis' makes us blame victims for their own misfortunes
angle: While just-world views are linked to extremist attitudes and specific brain activity, empathy for victims can reduce the tendency to blame them.
title: The Biology of Blame

hooks.text: Does your brain have a setting for justice?
You believe the world is fair. Your brain might agree.
You blame the victim to feel safe.
A blue light reflects on a scrolling screen.
Just-world beliefs are linked to extremist attitudes.

reveal.headline: Belief in a just world correlates with specific brain activity.
reveal.body: Research shows that belief in a just world is linked to activity in the insula and somatosensory cortex.

explain.headline: Just-world views are linked to extremist attitudes.
explain.body: Evidence shows a positive relationship between these beliefs and extremist attitudes. Violence narratives in online posts can heighten negativity bias and increase these views.

matters.headline: Policy can turn belief into blame.
matters.body: Government models have been used to justify victim-blaming in social welfare policies. That may be why you see certain groups blamed for their own lack of resources.

example.headline: A news feed on a late night train.
example.body: You scroll through headlines of violence. You feel a sense of order in the world. You think the people in the stories made their own choices.

question.headline: Who do you blame when someone suffers?

verdict: The evidence shows that just-world beliefs are linked to extremist attitudes and specific brain regions, and that government models have been used to justify victim-blaming in welfare policy.
caveat: The research on empathy and victim-blaming is specific to sexual harassment and does not necessarily generalize to all types of misfortunes.
caption:
Your belief in a fair world may be a biological and social construct.

Research links just-world views to specific brain activity and extremist attitudes. These views can be reinforced by online violence narratives and used to justify victim-blaming in welfare policy. Note that research on empathy and victim-blaming is specific to sexual harassment.
